Title: Diagnosis of test `testElementDOM` failure in `ExternalXMLNamespaceTest`

1. The test method `testElementDOM` calls `doTestElement` with the argument `DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM`.
2. The `doTestElement` method calls `doTest` with specific parameters: the XPath expression `"/ElementA/B:ElementB"`, the model string (here `MODEL_DOM`), and the expected value `"MY VALUE"`.
3. The `doTest` method creates a `JXPathContext` from a `DocumentContainer` instance, created by `createDocumentContainer(model)`. It then registers two namespaces `"A"` and `"B"` mapped to `"foo"` and `"bar"`, respectively. Finally, it asserts that the XPath expression evaluates to the expected string `"MY VALUE"`.
4. The `createDocumentContainer` method instantiates a `DocumentContainer` with a URL resource `"ExternalNS.xml"` and the model string. It also disables namespace awareness (calls `result.setNamespaceAware(false)`).
5. In the constructor of `DocumentContainer(URL xmlURL, String model)`, the provided URL and model are recorded.
6. Given the test failure involves an XPath expression referencing namespaced elements and namespaces are registered in the XPath context, the disabling of namespace awareness in the `DocumentContainer` (line 45) is suspicious. Disabling namespace awareness means the DOM model will not recognize or preserve namespaces.
7. This will cause XPath queries which rely on namespace prefixes to fail when executed on the DOM model, since elements will not have namespace information properly associated.

Hence, the root cause of the test failure is likely that disabling namespace awareness on the DOM model (`result.setNamespaceAware(false)`) causes the XPath lookup with namespaces to fail, resulting in an assertion error.

Recommended fix: Investigate why namespace awareness is disabled specifically for the DOM model in `createDocumentContainer`. Potentially, enable namespace awareness for the DOM model (and adjust related code if necessary) to allow XPath queries with namespaces to succeed.

---

The best methods to fix or investigate would be:

org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.ExternalXMLNamespaceTest.createDocumentContainer(java.lang.String)

org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.DocumentContainer.setNamespaceAware(boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
